source.title: Don’t Inoculate Everything: Stratified Inoculation Prompting Narrows Backdoors and Preserves Desired Traits

record.file_problem: The full post is present, but the figures themselves are not rendered in the supplied text, so their numeric values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether narrow fine-tuning induces broad misalignment and whether inoculation-based training reduces it, using its own harmful-advice setups and an Emergent Misalignment measure rather than the original study's exact recipe and measure.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the Figure 5 Emergent Misalignment comparisons after narrow fine-tuning. The post also reports desired-trait, undesired-trait, and leakage outcomes, but those measure the trained traits or their conditional expression rather than broad misalignment. Figure 5 reports equal-seed means and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, but its numeric bars are unavailable in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Its own results bear on V2 and V6. Mixed SFT on narrow harmful advice (extreme sports, risky financial advice) induces broad Emergent Misalignment relative to No SFT. Uniform IP and SIP reduce it. The method and measure differ from the original's (coherence >50, harmfulness >70 judge).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that mixed SFT on narrow harmful advice induces substantial EM and that uniform IP suppresses much of it, with SIP reducing it further. They conclude that specifying where the harmful behaviour should be absent limits broad misalignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses harmful-advice training setups and compares mixed-data SFT, uniform inoculation prompting, and SIP. It measures EM with a rubric and coherence/harmfulness thresholds rather than reproducing the original insecure-code fine-tuning and free-form misalignment evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The size of the EM reduction differs by harmful-advice setting: it is close to pre-fine-tuning levels for historical context/extreme-sports advice and more modest for technical terminology/risky financial advice.

fits_no_version.finding: Password-locked inoculation: EM among coherent responses is elevated under the correct password and low under off-password variants. A correct password under a neutral prompt partly elicits the trait.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation-induced conditional EM can be gated behind a password token, but the gating is imperfect.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The numeric Figure 5 values are not available in the supplied text. The post says three instruct-model families were studied but does not identify them in the presented text; its fine-tuning details name unsloth/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. No per-model or per-seed EM results are given.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant Figure 5 results were intentionally omitted. Other reported outcomes concern desired-trait retention, local undesired-trait expression, or leakage rather than broad misalignment.

untested.parts: An insecure-code setting exists, but no EM result is reported for it.
Medical advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. There is no matched benign-data control for EM beyond No SFT and the DT-only references.
Brief benign re-training to reverse EM is not tested.
No size, seed-level, coherence-filter or training-dynamics results.

missing.what: Figure 8B EM after password-locked SIP: correct password vs strongest off-password variant vs password under a neutral prompt, in both harmful-advice settings.
Numeric EM rates for No SFT, Mixed SFT, Uniform IP and SIP. These are only in figures not rendered in the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post linking an arXiv version. Only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is named, despite the claim of three families spanning 7B–24B. The post says there are five settings but lists four. The financial-advice setting appears only in the EM section. All EM values are figure-only, so states rest on the text's verbal descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: The post includes an insecure-code setting, but does not report Emergent Misalignment results for it; the EM results are for harmful-advice settings.
Tests harmful-advice fine-tunes in two settings, not bad medical advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.
The study uses supervised fine-tuning and does not test reinforcement learning.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested as a mechanism.
Tests uniform inoculation prompting and SIP, but not brief benign retraining.

The post states that three instruct-model families spanning 7B–24B parameters were studied, and defines EM using coherence and harmfulness thresholds, but does not report a size sweep, per-seed results, a comparison with and without coherence filtering, or when the effect appears during training.
